notes: Thirty-six environmental review documents, one per project, for the projects of 1974-1982 that the collection titles by project name rather than by street address - the group the earlier batches' filter (a title beginning with a digit) never reached. These are the same kind of document as the address-titled downtown reports already mined: one site, a historic-architectural chapter, and a rating index of the buildings on and around the block. The richest are One Sansome, the Bank of Canton headquarters, Russ Tower, the Daon Building, the Neiman-Marcus store and the Federal Reserve Bank, each of which dates and credits buildings that the project then removed. Ten of the thirty-six yielded nothing: the reports of 1974-1977 predate the historic-architectural chapter and mostly state that the site holds nothing listed in Here Today or designated by the Board of Supervisors.

coverage.remaining: The 1983-1987 named-site projects (18 more projects in this group), the 39 named-site projects of 1988-2005, and the other groups of the project-titled set: 50 documents whose titles carry a street address but not in first position, 130 area and policy plans, 77 institutional campus projects, 67 transportation and airport documents, 96 procedural notices and 35 documents about places outside San Francisco. See the dossier's triage note.
coverage.note: 36 documents read whole, one per project, the draft where a project has a draft and a final. Ten yielded nothing: the 1974 Carolina/Nineteenth/Wisconsin/Twentieth condominiums, Golden Gate Heights, the State Compensation Insurance Fund home office, 4050 17th Street, North Point Park/Marina, the Bank of America data processing centre garage, Stonestown, Welsh Commons, the Pine-Kearny office building, the Olympic Club Hotel and the Tai Associates Second and Harrison project all state that no listed or designated building is on or near the site. The scrambled two-column rating tables in the Holiday Inn and Hilton Tower No. 2 reports were read for names and refused for pairings: their columns arrive in the text layer interleaved, so only the buildings those reports also name in prose are recorded.

findings.description: The Alaska Commercial Building stood here from 1909 until the 1970s — designed three years earlier by Henry H. Meyers and Clarence Ward and built at a cost of about $500,000. Fourteen storeys on an L-shaped plan with its long side to Sansome Street, steel and reinforced concrete, its California, Sansome and Halleck Street elevations faced in granite and terra cotta and carved with walruses and marine motifs for the Alaska Commercial Company, whose offices it held.
